configProperties._comment_Server: Server GC with a BOUNDED heap count. Indexing runs at ProcessorCount - 1 and allocates a token array, a PToken stream, an AST and extraction builders per file, and under Workstation GC those threads serialise on one heap. Measured end to end on the real server, bo3, 1,085 files: 2.6-2.7 s with Workstation against 0.4-0.5 s with this. Raising the Workstation gen0 budget to 256 MB only reaches ~1,350 ms in the harness, so the contention is the heap count and not the collection frequency.
configProperties._comment_HeapCount: Eight. The heap count changes the PEAK while indexing and not the memory the server rests at, because Program.cs compacts the large-object heap once at the indexing to serving transition and that returns the pages: measured on the real server, four heaps rest at 125.4-125.9 MB, eight at 125.0-126.8 and one per core at 128.3-128.9, against Workstation's 127. Eight indexes in 0.4-0.5 s against four's 0.5-0.6 with a peak within a few MB of it; one per core is no faster and peaks at 392-453 MB. Retained memory is 55 MB at every setting.
configProperties._comment_LOHThreshold: 2 MB, not the default 85 KB. A heavy script's source text (a 98 KB file is a 196 KB string), its token arrays and a record's reference array all cross 85 KB, and the large-object heap is collected only by gen2: at 10,000 copies of the heaviest BO3 scripts it swung up to 3.3 GB during the cold index and took 72 gen2 collections. Measured cold-only at 10K, retained memory identical (2,109 MB) at every setting: default 19.0 s, 3.9 s paused, 72 gen2, 6.6 GB peak working set; 512 KB 13.5 s / 5.4 GB; 1 MB 9.1 s / 5.5 GB; 2 MB 7.5 s, 1.9 s paused, 4 gen2, 4.2 GB; 8 MB the same as 2 MB. At stock size (bo3, 1,000 files) 0.3 s against 0.4, and a transient peak of 648 MB against 383 that the post-index compaction returns.
